steps.title: Run functions concurrently with asyncio.gather
steps.instruction: In your main() function, replace the single await call with asyncio.gather() to run both my_async_function and second_async_function concurrently.
steps.hint: Use asyncio.gather() with both async function calls as arguments, preceded by await.

    result = await asyncio.gather(task1(), task2())

steps.title: Add error handling with try/except
steps.instruction: Wrap the await asyncio.gather() call inside your main() function with a try/except block to handle potential errors.
steps.hint: Use try: before the await call and except Exception as e: to catch any errors, then print the error.
steps.seedCode:
# Import the asyncio and time modules here
import asyncio
import time

# Define your async function here
async def my_async_function():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("First function completed")

# Create your second async function here
async def second_async_function():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("Second function completed")

# Create your main async function here
async def main():
    # Use asyncio.create_task() to start my_async_function as a background task
    
    # Call my_async_function with await here
    # Add print statement before asyncio.gather
    try:
        await asyncio.gather(my_async_function(), second_async_function())
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred: {e}")

# Call asyncio.run() to execute your main() function here
asyncio.run(main())
steps.expectedOutcome: Your main() function now includes error handling around the concurrent execution of async functions.
successCriteria: The await asyncio.gather() call is wrapped in a try/except block that catches Exception and prints the error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling to your async code. This ensures your program can handle unexpected errors gracefully.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the try/except block properly wraps the await asyncio.gather() call and includes an except clause that prints the error.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to wrap the await asyncio.gather() call in a try/except block to handle potential errors in the async execution.

steps.title: Add timing with time module
steps.instruction: In your main() function, use time.time() to measure and print the total execution time of your async program. Add code to record the start time before running your async functions and the end time after they complete, then calculate and print the duration.
steps.hint: Call time.time() at the beginning and end of your main() function, subtract to get the duration, and print it with a descriptive message.
steps.analogousExample:
# Example: timing a function
import time

async def timed_operation():
    start = time.time()
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    end = time.time()
    print(f"Operation took {end - start:.2f} seconds")

asyncio.run(timed_operation())
